title: Empty the Mind
coreMove: A clear mind is not blank; it sorts each loop by control, cuts fresh input at the door, and returns attention to the next thing you can do now.

exampleSpecs.domain: late transit after a noisy dinner
exampleSpecs.audience: commuters carrying input noise into the next choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: One person keeps feeding attention with screens while another sorts what can be acted on.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two people face the same platform noise and diverge by sorting control differently.

exampleSpecs.audience: workers stuck rehearsing an outcome they cannot govern
exampleSpecs.stakes: A crew can waste its prep time fearing weather instead of protecting seedlings.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A mentor reframes a stuck view with a quotable control sentence.

exampleSpecs.audience: learners who confuse control sorting with giving up
exampleSpecs.stakes: A trainee may hear the Stoic split as passivity unless confusion is used as teaching material.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The learner's confusion becomes the path into Epictetus's controllable and uncontrollable split.

exampleSpecs.audience: competitors who turn posted rankings into mental loops
exampleSpecs.stakes: A fixed lane assignment can either start rumination or cue the next controllable action.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same person meets the same lane board with one variable changed: the control question.

exampleSpecs.audience: clinical teams looking for hidden attention drains
exampleSpecs.stakes: Ambient screens may be treated as harmless until work records show where attention leaked.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A quiet review of logs reveals one concrete screen-driven pattern.

exampleSpecs.audience: hands-on workers caught in replay while solving a physical problem
exampleSpecs.stakes: A simple parts run can become an inner trial unless the worker returns to controllable steps.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Stay inside one person's thought process with no external dialogue.
